### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-5.mdx`  _(via AuditPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 495a79c7b38c82b4ca4c840b387626b6a1a4b16e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `10520036599bdf242ebb1eaeead9b5cc76fea424` — the merge of head `34600be3f54e9a41bffd21abc8b52ff3be4bb86c` into base `495a79c7b38c82b4ca4c840b387626b6a1a4b16e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 10520036599bdf242ebb1eaeead9b5cc76fea424 && git checkout 10520036599bdf242ebb1eaeead9b5cc76fea424
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 495a79c7b38c82b4ca4c840b387626b6a1a4b16e 34600be3f54e9a41bffd21abc8b52ff3be4bb86c && git checkout -B drift-repro 495a79c7b38c82b4ca4c840b387626b6a1a4b16e && git merge --no-ff 34600be3f54e9a41bffd21abc8b52ff3be4bb86c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 495a79c7b38c82b4ca4c840b387626b6a1a4b16e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 495a79c7b38c82b4ca4c840b387626b6a1a4b16e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 verdict: ACCEPT** · PR #34495 · card #34280 · first review · read 2026-11-16T23:51Z

Head-sha: `34600be3f54e9a41bffd21abc8b52ff3be4bb86c` (the head named in final-head comment 6932977335)

Read from GitHub at this head (`get_files`, diff, check-runs), not from the report.

**Checklist**
- Shape: draft, base `main`; the body opens with the attribution lines and then `Fixes #34280`. The whole card is delivered. No other card number is in the body.
- Scope: 4 files: `plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts`, `audit-seal/sealer.ts`, one new integration test, and a root changeset. No `content/docs/releases/`. The docs-drift advisory names pages only through the `AuditPlugin` symbol; none of them states the seam-resolution rule changed here.
- Changeset: root, patch for `@objectstack/plugin-audit` (published). I checked each sentence against the diff:
  - "It turned every resolution error into 'not registered'" matches `main`'s `optional()` helper, whose bare `catch` returned `undefined`.
  - "A seam registered as a factory was never built at all, because the sealer used the synchronous accessor" matches the old `ctx.getService`; the new `hostSeamResolver` uses `kernel.getServiceAsync`.
  - "only an absent seam falls back" matches: only `isServiceNotRegisteredError` (exported from `@objectstack/core`) maps to `undefined`, and every other rejection rethrows.
  - "stops the pass … reports it at `error`, naming the slot, once while it lasts. Each pass retries" matches `resolveSeams()` returning `null`, `runPass` answering 0, `report('resolve:<slot>')`, and the key cleared on the next successful resolve.
- Tests: the new file runs a real `ObjectKernel` with ObjectQL over SQLite (wasm), with 5 cases. Case 1 is the control (absent seam, local key, no error); it also proves the branded not-registered path on a real kernel, since no sink or cluster is registered in it. The absorbing cases assert 0 checkpoints, no local key minted, and one `error` line naming the slot, and none on a second pass. The recorded ablation (fix reverted, test kept) turns cases 2–5 red and leaves case 1 green.
- Gates: 51 check-runs on this head, all `completed`: 35 `success`, 16 `skipped`, 0 failed. Lint & Repo Gates `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`, Test Core 1–8 `success`, Build Core `success`, Check Changeset `success`, Governed Surface Queue Guard `success`. The skips are the UI and opt-in jobs a server-only diff does not trigger.

**Spot checks (mine)**
1. `AuditSealer` and `AuditSealerOptions` are not re-exported from `src/index.ts` or `src/audit-seal/index.ts`, and the package `exports` map has only `.`. So the option getters' widened return type (`T | Promise<T>`) is not a published-surface change.
2. Seams are now resolved once per pass and handed down. `acquireLock(cluster)` no longer swallows a throwing getter, and `ObjectPass.deliver` uses the pass's resolved sink. A sink whose `deliver()` rejects is still only a `warn`, as on `main`.
3. Ordering: `plans()` returns first, so a deployment with nothing to seal never resolves seams and gets no new error line.
4. Without crypto and without a host signer, `signer` resolves to `undefined` and the existing `no-crypto` report fires, unchanged.

**Narrowing declaration: agreed, `Clause-②: no` with no `(narrowing)` arm.** No key, config value, or service shape a host or author writes is refused. What changes is the reaction to a registration that already fails at resolution: a silent fallback becomes a stopped pass with an `error` line. That is the card's rule. A host with a working registration sees no change. A factory-registered seam that resolves is now used where it was ignored, which repairs the stated D11 contract rather than widening it. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right too: nothing a metadata author writes changes.

**Outside this PR, owed:** `packages/cli/src/utils/audit-redaction-seal.ts` still resolves `AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_SIGNER_SERVICE` / `AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_SINK_SERVICE` through a catch-all helper (bare `catch` at :60, consumed at :67), so a CLI redaction run with a failing host signer still falls back to the local signer. It is outside the claimed file surface, so it is correctly left alone here; the seat files the follow-up card.

**L2 owed: no.** None of the four contract faces is touched: `Clause-②: no`, no narrowing (agreed above), no `packages/spec/src/**` path, no governed rule text.

**Landing tier**: `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34495` reports 0 of 4 paths governed and +326/−30 = 356 lines ≤ 3000. Ordinary queue landing by the area at this head.
